title: LightTrack SDK contract fixtures
description: One machine-readable description of the behaviour every LightTrack client SDK must share. Each file under fixtures/ is a case list; the per-language runners (clients/rust/tests/contract.rs, clients/typescript/src/contract.test.ts, clients/python/tests/test_contract.py) load ALL of them and assert. A behaviour that is not in a fixture is not part of the contract; a behaviour that is may not differ between languages.

usage.description: What every extractor must return from a native provider response.

why.description: Why this shape is in the contract.

response.description: A real captured provider response body.

guardRules.description: Rules in neutral snake_case. Each runner maps them onto its own rules type (the TypeScript SDK's public field names stay camelCase; only the wire form here is normalised).

violations.description: The FAILED check keys, sorted. Keys are snake_case in every language: json, key:<k>, max_words, min_words, max_chars, include:<s>, must_match, not_match:<pattern>, no_pii, pii:<kind>. Violation MESSAGES are deliberately not part of the contract - they are prose and are allowed to read naturally per language.

body.description: A journal file body, newline-delimited JSON. Records are {"o":"b","k":<key>,...} on open and {"o":"e","k":<key>} on settle.

expect.description: The unsettled open records, in file order. Compared on the fields present here only, so a runner may carry extras.

status.description: HTTP status of the ingest response.

body.description: Parsed response body, or null when there was none.

expect.description: The parsed limit view. Parse only - acting on it is the `admission` list.

binding_scope.description: The dimension the worst rule applies to. `null` means project-wide.

binding_rule.description: Id of the worst rule - the key the shed lottery hashes against.

admissionCase.description: One pre-spend admission decision. The runner builds a fresh admission cache with `ttl_ms`, replays every `observe` entry through the SDK's limit-view parser at its `at_ms`, then asks `admit` at its own `at_ms` and compares the verdict. Time is supplied, never read from a clock, so the case is a pure function in all three languages.

ttl_ms.description: How long a view stays evidence. Default 30000.

observe.description: Ingest responses the SDK has already seen, in order.

name.description: Use-case of the call about to be made, matched against a `name`-scoped view.

event_id.description: Id the call would be recorded under. Required for the shed lottery; without it shedding cannot be decided and never refuses.

ok.description: Whether the provider call should be made.

reason.description: `null` when ok. `retry_after` = a 429's advertised wait has not elapsed; `at_cap` = usage_ratio >= 1.0; `shed` = the deterministic shed lottery picked this event.

retry_after_secs.description: Only set for `retry_after`: a client must not invent a back-off the server never promised.

stale.description: The view is older than `ttl_ms`, so the verdict was taken without current evidence (and therefore admits). The caller's cue to refresh from GET /v1/limits/status.

shedLotteryCase.description: One point of the shed lottery (ARCHITECTURE §7c): FNV-1a over rule_id + 0x1f + event_id, SplitMix64 avalanche, top 53 bits over 2^53. Pinned because a client running a different hash still sheds proportionally and still looks right in aggregate, while disagreeing with the server on every individual event.

ticket.description: The point in [0, 1). The event is shed iff this is below the rule's shed_fraction.

status.description: null means the request never reached the server (network error / timeout).

kind.description: Rate-limiting bucket the SDK warns under.

hint_contains.description: Substrings the composed failure message must contain in EVERY language. The full sentence is prose; these are the load-bearing parts (what went wrong, what to set).

pattern.description: Restricted to the RE2 / JavaScript / Python / Rust common subset: no lookaround, no backreferences.

pii.description: GENERATED by crates/anon/src/export.rs. Do not hand-edit.
